# M1 Test-Data Library — Master Index

All data is fictional and synthetic. No real company (including any employer) data was used. Generated with free tools only (Python standard library) by `tests/tools/library/build.py`, which writes 205 of this library's 206 files; `MANIFEST.sha256` is not produced by the generator. A fresh rebuild on 12 Nov 2026 (Python 3.13.18, Linux 6.18) reproduced 203 of the 205 generated files byte for byte; the other two, this index and Package 06 `E08-duplicate-records/EXPECTED.md`, contain hand-written text and so differ from a freshly generated version. Only that Python version and environment have been tested. Reproducing the files shows they match the generator; it does not show that the generated expected results are correct. The v1.0 ZIPs, including `00-Generator-Scripts.zip`, are superseded by v1.0.2 (see `M1-DESIGN.md`, "Test-data library: repository content and delivered ZIPs").

## How the expected results were produced

`refcalc.py` reads only the CSVs in each package and applies the documented reference formulas. It does not use the generator's internal values, so it checks what is actually in the files. Edge cases also have hand-specified expectations. For 02, figures are calculated on `expected-canonical/`, the data as it should be after the importer applies every documented action. Some of these expectations rest on fixture assumptions, which are not approved business rules. (1) Conflicting duplicates (02: I09 stock, I16 sales). The stop rule is decided: the affected import stops until the user names the row to keep (`M1-DESIGN.md`, "Conflicting duplicates"). Only the row choices are fixture assumptions: the figures assume the choices stated in `02-Messy-Manufacturer/DATA-ISSUES.md` (I09: the stock row with QOH 95, not 132; I16: the sales row with Qty Sold 94, not 103). These choices are not yet stored in a machine-readable resolution record; its format is a Stage 2 design decision. (2) Identical duplicates: the fixtures assume one copy is kept for Package 02 I08 and I19 (each pair byte-identical in every source column) and for the duplicate stock, PO line and item records in Package 06 E08, and the expected import-report counts depend on this. Whether identical duplicates may be removed is open decision A6; if A6 is decided differently, the affected expected outputs change only through a separately approved change. The conflicting demand row in E08 is separate: it stops the affected import under an already-decided rule (`M1-DESIGN.md`, "Package 06 E08 — interpretation (a)") and is not an A6 assumption. See `M1-DESIGN.md`, "Identical duplicates" and "Known gap in Package 02's expected results".

## Check against today's engine (12 Nov 2026, commit 3e5a7b3, time zone UTC)

A throwaway prototype converted 01 and 04 into the Northstar eight-sheet layout and ran `CGEngine.runEngine()`. This is evidence about today's engine, not the M1 importer.

- **01 Clean Manufacturer:** runs without error. The engine rates S07 Kestrel Castings High risk (score 54). P0007, P0019 and P0031 have cover below lead time (2.5 vs 5.1, 3.0 vs 10.3, 4.5 vs 14.4 days). It also reports one High data-quality message: raw-material on-order in stock differs from PO outstanding by 2,030 units across 7 materials. Cause: today's engine treats a part-received PO line that has a receipt date as fully closed, so its undelivered balance is not counted as on order. See the M1 design, Deliverable 4.
- **04 Mixed Make/Buy:** runs, but bought-in products R0003 and R0006 get an assumed 7-day lead time ("Assumed (default setting)") and about 14 days of cover, so they are NOT flagged. Their purchase orders are reported as "unknown supplier/material", and R-items are reported as "Products with no BOM". This is the expected failure that the proposed Make/Buy change must fix.

## Delivered copies

The delivered copies are the v1.0.2 ZIPs: packages 01 to 06 and the generator scripts, captured from the repository files of M1 pre-tag Commit 2 (`77621b0`). They show the library as it was at that commit, not necessarily the current repository. The v1.0 ZIPs are superseded. Keep the delivered ZIPs unchanged as a record of what was delivered at that commit. For the test-data library, the current repository is the source of truth: where repository contents and a delivered ZIP differ, the repository version is authoritative. This index and `MANIFEST.sha256` exist only in the repository and are not in any ZIP. See `M1-DESIGN.md`, "Test-data library: repository content and delivered ZIPs", and the ZIP checksums in `tests/V07-TEST-RECORD.md`.
